name: Peony Red
lede: Peony red is a dark red, named for the flower, with a few appearances in textile description.

sections.title: A flower's red
sections.body:
Paterson defines peony red as a dark red, and lists it with the reds, among them [[maroon]] and mulberry [1]. Its sibling in the pinks is *peony pink*, the pink of the same flower [1]. Paterson also records *pæonin*, defined only as a red colour [1].

A use in textile description comes from Finlay: a V&A monograph described a kani-woven pashmina fragment with yellow tulips in a color list that begins with peony red, verdigris and cinnamon [2]. The fragment is among the earliest known kani weaving and had been kept in the dark for nearly two centuries, so the colors survived [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of museum paintings, a color near this swatch is present in 135 works, 0.57 per cent of the archive [3]. The earliest is a work of 1368 and the latest dates from 1947 [3]. Within the archive it is about 3.4 times more common after 1490 than before, as photographed [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
